mechanism_narrative: A lower Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as lower rates reduce the cost of capital and increase equity valuations. This relationship is consistent across the observed data range without requiring a threshold condition.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 5-day forward returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy cycle that compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) drives S&P 500 returns: when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls, it signals a 'soft landing' scenario that produces positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This interaction is non-additive and requires both series to move in the specified directions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases > 0.25% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.25% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.25% in the last 3 months, or Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.5%), a decline in the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as the central bank is likely to pursue accommodative policies to stimulate the economy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.5% and FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as higher unemployment signals a potential economic slowdown that leads to central bank rate cuts and increased equity valuations.
failure_condition: Rank IC between UNRATE and 60-day forward returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.5%, it signals a high-unemployment regime that leads to central bank rate cuts and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between real GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) drives S&P 500 returns: when real GDP growth is slowing and housing starts are declining, it signals a potential economic downturn that produces negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This interaction is non-additive and requires both series to move in the specified directions.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate decreases > 0.5% in 3 months and HOUST decreases > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth rate decreases > 0.5% and HOUST decreases > 0.5% in the last 3 months, or Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 110, it signals a potential economic slowdown that produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This signal is active only in low-industrial-production regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 110, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
